requirement_text.ISS-0292: Letflow.SandboxPoolTest RT-9/RT-8 flaked on GitHub Actions CI with Postgres query_canceled + orphaned sandbox schema -- likely CPU-throttled-runner timeout, needs investigation. ISSUE-FIXER's Step 1 diagnosis (see handoffs/escalations.yaml run_id WF03-ISS0292-20260823) confirmed a real, generalizable defect in test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs: (1) query_without_holding/1 (:513-531) runs fun.() in a bare spawn_monitor with no rescue -- a Repo.query! that raises Postgrex.Error{postgres: %{code: :query_canceled}} crashes the spawned process, and the :DOWN branch turns that into flunk/1 which raises in the caller (including inside on_exit callbacks). (2) drop_sandbox_schemas_created_since!/1 (:552-560)'s `for schema_name <- MapSet.difference(...) do query_without_holding(...) end` has no per-iteration rescue -- one flunk raised inside the loop body propagates straight out of the whole for, so every schema ordered after the failing one in that diff set is NEVER attempted (the RT-8 orphan leak). Acceptance criteria: (a) determine one-off vs recurring (a scan of the last 5 CI runs on main already found zero recurrence of this exact signature -- cite that, do not need to redo it); (b) if query_canceled can recur, make cleanup retry-tolerant of a cancelled statement OR raise the timeout for the cleanup path specifically; (c) ensure a cancelled/interrupted cleanup cannot leave an orphaned sandbox schema behind for a LATER test -- this is the critical one; (d) if purely transient, note as documented known-flaky rather than leaving open indefinitely -- not applicable here since a real code defect was confirmed independent of recurrence.

task.description:
THIS IS A RESTART AFTER MAX_REWORK ESCALATION (see handoffs/escalations.yaml, run_id WF03-ISS0292-20260823, escalated_at 2026-08-23T08:05:46Z). Three prior design iterations at lib/letflow/design/iss0292-sandbox-pool-test-cleanup-resilience.md (still on this branch, read it for what NOT to repeat) each stacked a NEW timeout/retry budget one layer further out to patch the previous iteration's gap: pass 1's retry-once-at-44s could total 88s vs the 45s outer pool_op_rendezvous_timeout(); pass 2 widened that outer bound to 89s per call site but then exceeded ExUnit's untouched 60s default per-test timeout; pass 3 added a 120s @moduletag timeout sized against a single-call worst case, but RT-1..RT-5 call the cleanup helpers MORE THAN ONCE per test body, so two stuck calls alone (178s) still exceed 120s. Do NOT attempt a 4th arithmetic patch of this shape.

Instead, use this specific alternative strategy (a synthesis of escalation options (a)/(c)): the retry must happen INSIDE the already-existing per-call timeout budget, not by adding a new outer layer.

1. Add a small retry wrapper used ONLY around the two raw Repo.query! call sites inside sandbox_schema_names/0 (:538-545) and inside drop_sandbox_schemas_created_since!/1's DROP call (:554-556) -- rescue Postgrex.Error and DBConnection.ConnectionError, retry the SAME query exactly once with NO explicit :timeout override (so it uses Postgrex's own client-side default, ~15_000ms, same as today -- do not introduce a new named timeout constant). This retry happens INSIDE the process spawned by query_without_holding/1, so it is already bounded by query_without_holding/1's existing pool_op_rendezvous_timeout() (45_000ms today) with no change to that constant, no change to @moduletag, no change to ExUnit's default per-test timeout. Two ~15s attempts (30s) comfortably fits inside the existing unmodified 45s outer bound -- verify and state this arithmetic explicitly in the design (this is the fix for the RT-9 root symptom: an isolated query_canceled now self-heals on retry without ever reaching flunk).
2. Separately and independently, fix drop_sandbox_schemas_created_since!/1's for-loop so ONE schema's cleanup failure (after the retry above is exhausted -- i.e. a genuinely stuck DROP, not transient noise) does NOT abort the whole loop and leave later schemas in the diff set unattempted. Reuse the rescue-log-and-continue shape test/support/tenant_schema_reaper.ex's reclaim_row/1 already establishes in this codebase (rescue, Logger.warning, return a boolean, never raise from the per-item body) rather than inventing a new shape. After attempting every schema in the diff set, if any genuinely failed twice (retry exhausted), raise ONE combined failure citing all of them -- this still surfaces a genuinely-stuck resource loudly (per the original design's own stated rationale: two real failures at existing-timeout each is evidence of something actually stuck, not scheduling jitter) while guaranteeing every OTHER schema in the diff set was still attempted regardless of one failure (this is what closes acceptance criterion (c), the orphan-for-a-later-test gap -- RT-8's exact failure mode).
3. Explicitly verify and state in the design: zero existing timeout/retry constants change value (pool_op_rendezvous_timeout(), release_call_timeout(), provision_timeout_ms(), ExUnit's default per-test timeout, no new @moduletag). This is the property that makes this design immune to the three-layer stacking failure the prior three iterations hit -- say so explicitly with the arithmetic (2x ~15s retry <= existing 45s bound, with margin stated) rather than asserting it.
4. Independently confirm (per WF-03 Step 0.5 discipline already partially done by ISSUE-FIXER) this remains TEST CODE ONLY -- no lib/ file, no migration, no config/*.exs touched. State the verification, don't just inherit the claim from the prior design doc.

Write the design to a NEW file (do not silently overwrite the rejected doc's history -- either append a clearly-marked 'Pass 4 (post-escalation restart)' section to the existing lib/letflow/design/iss0292-sandbox-pool-test-cleanup-resilience.md file recording why passes 1-3 were rejected and what pass 4 does differently, or start fresh and cross-reference -- your call, but the prior three passes' findings must remain readable, not deleted). Exact file-by-file / line-level change list required. No implementation code -- describe the rescue/retry shape precisely enough for ELIXIR-DEV or TEST-DESIGNER to implement without further design decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Design explicitly rejects a 4th outer-timeout-widening patch and states why (references the 3 prior FAILs)
Retry happens inside the existing pool_op_rendezvous_timeout() budget with no change to that constant's value, and the arithmetic proving it fits is shown
No new or widened @moduletag timeout, no change to ExUnit's default per-test timeout
drop_sandbox_schemas_created_since!/1's loop continues past one schema's cleanup failure (post-retry) rather than aborting the whole for -- reusing tenant_schema_reaper.ex's rescue-log-continue shape
A genuinely-stuck schema (fails twice) still surfaces as a real, loud test failure -- not silently swallowed
Independently re-verifies TEST CODE ONLY scope (no lib/, no migration, no config/*.exs)
Exact file-by-file / line-level change list for test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs
No implementation code in the design artefact
Prior three rejected passes remain readable (appended-to or cross-referenced, not deleted)

The sole defect was that Sections 9.3, 9.4, and 9.5 contained near-compilable Elixir code (real fn/case/if/rescue bodies with concrete variable names), which is implementation code and contradicted Section 9.11's own claim that no such body was given verbatim. Rewrote ONLY 9.3, 9.4, and 9.5 down to @spec-level signatures plus prose description of control flow and rationale, matching the prose/@spec-only style Sections 3.1-3.4 (the 3 rejected earlier passes) already used and that the validator confirmed was correct. 9.3 (sandbox_schema_names/0) now describes in prose that its Repo.query! call is passed as the fun argument to retry_query_once/1, with the result flowing into the same unchanged row-to-MapSet conversion, and that the unmodified :DOWN-to-flunk crash path still fires on exhausted retry (no loop to protect) -- no fenced code block containing a real function body. 9.4 (resilient_drop_schema/1) now describes in prose the single added rescue clause sitting outside retry_query_once/1, converting an exhausted retry to {:error, exception} instead of letting it propagate, matching TenantSchemaReaper.reclaim_row/1's shape -- no fn/rescue code block. 9.5 (drop_sandbox_schemas_created_since!/1) now describes in prose the accumulating walk over schemas_to_drop that attempts every schema exactly once, collects {schema_name, reason} pairs for failures, and raises one combined flunk/1 after the full pass if any accumulated, modeled on TenantSchemaReaper.sweep_orphans/2's accumulate-and-continue shape -- no Enum.reduce/case code block. Updated Section 9.11's 'No implementation code in the design' traceability row so its claim is now actually true: it now states that 9.2-9.5 give only @spec signatures plus prose, with no fenced Elixir syntax block containing a real fn/case/if/rescue function body appearing anywhere in Section 9, matching the style CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR already confirmed for 3.1-3.4. Did not touch the arithmetic in 9.6, the OQ-4 discussion in 9.7, the scope reverification in 9.8, or Sections 0-8, per the rework directive's explicit scope limits.
